02 / 04 · Ideas into structure

FOLD

A place for the pieces.

the idea

Fold explores how a workspace can bring writing, organizing, and doing closer together. A page becomes the starting point for a note, a project, or a shared piece of work.

Working project · local release materials
The project

Workspace & product exploration

My focus

Product exploration, interface design & implementation

At a glance

Block-based writing · Tasks & views · Collaborative pages

The starting point

Give an idea
somewhere to land.

A note can become a task, and a task can lead back to a document. Fold explores those connections through a workspace built around pages and editable blocks.

Studying established workspace products helped frame the questions. The interesting work was deciding how those ideas should fit together in a usable interface.

Organizing the work

A page is only
the beginning.

Pages provide a hierarchy for writing and knowledge. Tasks can be understood through table, board, list, and calendar views, with the same underlying work seen from different angles.

The project also explores shared page editing, permissions, comments, search, and recovery. These capabilities create the need for clear boundaries as well as convenient interactions.

A smaller window

The structure
comes with you.

Mobile views make the hierarchy especially important. Navigation, content, and task actions need to remain understandable within a much smaller space.

From voice to a page

Capture first.
Shape the note next.

The voice-notes workflow begins with recording. After recording stops, audio can be transcribed, reviewed, and developed into structured notes when the required service is configured.

The workflow keeps the transcript available as a source. Enhanced notes are reviewed before insertion into the page. Saved points stay tied to supporting quotes from the source material.

The product lesson

Complexity needs
a clear home.

Fold brings together many connected decisions: what belongs to a page, where tasks live, and how shared work remains understandable.

The ongoing challenge is to keep those decisions coherent across navigation, editing, and smaller screens. That is where the product continues to evolve.
